FLATBREAD WITH BUTTER CHICKEN #food #recipe #chicken #butterchicken #flatbread CHICKEN MIXTURE 25 g unsalted butter 20 ml sunflower oil 600 g chicken thighs, cut into cubes 5 g garam masala (1⅔ tsp) 2 g ground coriander (⅔ tsp) 2 g ground cumin (⅔ tsp) 3 g garlic powder (1 tsp) 4 g onion powder (1⅓ tsp) 2 g cayenne pepper (⅔ tsp) 30 g tomato paste 50 ml water 100 ml heavy cream 15 g honey 1 chicken stock cube 100 g grated cheese (Gouda) DOUGH 350 g all-purpose flour 50 g herb cream cheese 4 g salt (⅔ tsp) 6 g baking powder 170 ml water EXTRA cheese slices Heat the butter and sunflower oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken thighs, garam masala, ground coriander, ground cumin, garlic powder, onion powder, and cayenne pepper. Fry for 5–6 minutes. Add the tomato paste, water, cream, and honey. Mix well and let simmer for 5–7 minutes until the sauce has slightly thickened. Crumble the chicken stock cube over the pan. Add the grated cheese and stir until creamy. Remove from the heat and let the chicken mixture cool completely. Place the flour, baking powder, herb cream cheese, salt, and water in a large bowl. Knead for 10–12 minutes until smooth. Cover and let the dough rest for 10 minutes. Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces of about 70 g each and shape into balls. Roll out a dough ball into a circle. Place a slice of cheese on one half and spread about 90 g of the chicken mixture on top. Lightly moisten the edges, fold the dough closed, and press the edges firmly to seal. Place the filled dough on a sheet of parchment paper. Heat a heavy-bottomed frying pan with a little oil. Cook the breads over medium-high heat until golden brown and cooked through on both sides. Tips Don’t cut the chicken too small. Cubes of about 2 cm give a better bite. Let the mixture thicken well. The sauce should be creamy and firm, not runny like a curry. Let it cool completely. A warm filling makes the dough soft and hard to seal. Letting the dough rest is important. Those 10 minutes make it more elastic and easier to roll out. Use any cheese you like. You can also bake these breads in the oven. Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F) and bake for 15–20 minutes (brush with oil or butter). Add salt to taste. Preparation Time Chicken mixture preparation & cooling: 20 minutes Dough preparation & resting: 25 minutes Cooking: 10–15 minutes

For the Chicken:  -2 large chicken breasts, flattened  -Seasoning: 1 tbsp paprika, 2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp onion powder, 2 tsp Italian seasoning, 2 tsp salt, 2 tsp black pepper, 1–2 tsp cayenne pepper (optional)  -1 tbsp olive oil For the Pasta & Sauce:  -8 oz (225 g) rigatoni  -3 tbsp butter  -1 large shallot, finely diced  -6–8 garlic cloves, minced  -1 cup heavy cream, room temperature  -Seasoning: 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp garlic powder, 1 tsp Italian seasoning, 1 tsp black pepper  -3/4 cup freshly grated Parmesan (please use fresh!)  -1/2 cup pasta water, as needed (aka liquid gold) Instructions: 1. Sear for 3–4 mins per side until golden, then reduce heat if needed and cook through. Set aside to rest. 4. Reduce heat to medium. In the same pan, melt the butter, scraping up all that fond. Ingredients For the Chicken 1.5 lbs chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces 1 teaspoon each onion powder, garlic powder, and teaspoon salt ½ teaspoon each black pepper and paprika  2 tablespoons olive oil About ⅓ cup cornstarch Olive oil, for cooking For the Sticky Sauce ½ cup soy sauce ⅓ cup brown sugar or honey 1 tablespoon hoisin sauce 1 tablespoon ketchup 1 teaspoon ginger paste ½ tablespoon minced garlic 1 tablespoon cornstarch 2 tablespoons butter For Serving Cooked white rice Sliced green onions Sesame seeds Instructions 1. Add the chicken to a large bowl and season with onion powder, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, and paprika. Add 2 tablespoons of olive oil and toss until the chicken is evenly coated. 2. Tender stewed chicken and gravy recipe: Cook time: 80-90 mins  Servings: 6 Ingredients:  1/2 yellow onion  1/2 green bell pepper  1/2 red bell pepper  4 crushed garlic cloves  1/2 stick butter or olive oil  2 TBSP All purpose flour   6-8 boneless skinless chicken thighs  4 cups of chicken broth  Dried parsley  Seasonings: all purpose seasoning (such as natures seasoning or lawrys) onion & garlic powders, paprika, Italian seasoning, black pepper and if you don’t mind some spice toss in some Slap ya mama.  Directions: Season about 6-8 boneless skinless chicken thighs (depending on how many you’re serving) with all named seasonings. Marinate from 1 hour up to overnight. The longer the better. Use a Dutch oven or stock pot to sear the chicken in 2 TBSP of butter or olive oil. Sear for about 2-3 mins on each side on a medium high heat.  Remove chicken from pot. If you see little dark bits and pieces at the bottom of the pot leave it. It’s not burnt. That’s flavor that you want to keep in your pot to make the meal even more flavorful. It will deglaze and cook into the stew once you add your chicken broth.  In the same pot (without washing) on a medium heat add 1-2 TBSP of butter (depending on how much oil or butter you have left from searing the chicken). Add your peppers, onions and seasonings and cook down your peppers and onions for about 8-10 mins or until tender.  Once tender while still on a medium heat add in 1 TBSP of butter and whisk in 2 tbsp of flour to make a roux. Whisk frequently. Don’t walk away from your roux because this is A quick roux and can burn easily so watch it closely.  After about 5 mins you should have the color roux you want your gravy to be. For example if you want a dark brown gravy that roux should be dark brown.  After you’ve achieved that color add in 3 cups of chicken broth 1 cup at a time while stirring in between each cup. Season to taste with named seasonings.  Add in 3-4 crushed garlic cloves and a hefty TBSP of parsley. Put the lid on partially to bring this gravy to a simmer on a medium heat.  After about 10 mins add your chicken in and let it cook on a medium heat for 1 hour. Check it every 10 mins to make sure it doesn’t need more liquid. After your chicken is tender to your preference serve over rice or however you prefer.  **I served mine over white rice with loose, seasoned buttery corn and A blueberry loaf bread I made in the oven using Martha white blueberry cheesecake mix. Chicken Chasseur, the pan sauce way 🍄🍷 Classic French “hunter’s style” chicken, made the way it started out: a sauté with the sauce built in the same pan. Crisp skin, tender meat taken to 80°C, and a glossy mushroom, tomato, wine and tarragon sauce. Serves 2 INGREDIENTS  600g bone-in, skin-on chicken legs 1 tsp fine sea salt 1 tbsp light olive oil (optional, see step 3) 15g butter + 25g cold butter, cubed 120g chestnut mushrooms, halved or quartered 2 shallots, finely chopped 2 garlic cloves, finely chopped 1 tbsp tomato purée 2 tbsp brandy (optional) 150ml dry white wine 200ml chicken stock 2 ripe tomatoes 1 tbsp each chopped tarragon and parsley ½ tsp black pepper METHOD  1️⃣ Salt the chicken (no pepper yet, it burns). Pat dry after 10 mins, or dry brine uncovered on a rack in the fridge for 12 to 24 hrs.  2️⃣ Oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Blanch the tomatoes for around 60 seconds, plunge into iced water, then peel, deseed and dice.  3️⃣ Sear skin side down until deep golden. Either in hot oil, or my way: a cold stainless steel pan, low heat, no oil, so the chicken fries in its own fat. Be patient; if it sticks, it’ll release once browned.  4️⃣ Flip and roast until the thickest part hits 80°C. It’s safe at 75°C, but at 80°C the collagen breaks down for more tender meat.  5️⃣ Turn the oven off, door open until it drops to 50 to 60°C, then rest the chicken on a rack inside, uncovered.  6️⃣ Pour off all but 1 tbsp fat. Brown the mushrooms in the 15g butter over high heat, hard and fast, to drive off the steam.  7️⃣ Medium heat: soften the shallots, then add the garlic and tomato purée for 1 min.  8️⃣ Add the brandy and let it bubble away, then the wine. Scrape up the browned bits and reduce by half.  9️⃣ Add the stock, tomatoes and the chicken’s resting juices. Simmer until reduced by a third.  🔟 Off the heat, swirl in the cold butter, then the herbs and pepper. Taste and adjust the salt. Spoon the sauce onto the plate and sit the chicken on top so the skin stays crisp. Lovely with buttered leeks 🍂 Save this for a cosy autumn dinner 📌 #chickenchasseur #pansauce #frenchcooking #chickenrecipes

CHICKEN AU POIVRE 🇫🇷🔥 I genuinely wonder if the French are so fed up with people butchering their cuisine that they’ve started rioting in Paris. Perhaps this recipe was the final straw. Anyway, I’m convinced you could add cream to literally ANYTHING and it would taste good. BUT IT TASTES EVEN BETTER WHEN YOU ADD ALL THE SPICES LISTED BELOW. 🤓 Crispy, beautifully seasoned chicken thighs smothered in a rich, creamy peppercorn sauce, served alongside perfectly seasoned potato wedges. If you’re on a diet LIKE ME, I suggest you look away because we’re not counting calories today. 🤝 INGREDIENTS For the Chicken: 8–9 chicken thighs 2 tsp paprika 1 tsp smoked paprika 2 tsp onion powder 2 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp dried thyme 1½ tsp dried rosemary 1 chicken bouillon cube, crumbled Olive oil Salt, to taste 🥛 For the Creamy Peppercorn Sauce: 400g single cream 4–5 tbsp coarsely ground black pepper 1 red onion or shallot, finely chopped 4 garlic cloves, minced 1 tbsp freshly chopped rosemary 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce 1 tsp vinegar ½ tsp yellow mustard or Dijon mustard 1 cup chicken stock or water For the Potato Wedges: 6–7 🙂 small potatoes 1 tsp paprika 2 tsp onion powder 2 tsp dried parsley 3–4 tbsp olive oil Salt, to taste METHOD: 1️⃣ Marinate the Chicken  Add your chicken thighs to a bowl along with all the chicken seasonings and a drizzle of olive oil. Give everything a good mix, making sure every piece is thoroughly coated. Leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes, although the longer you leave it, the better the flavour. 🤝 2️⃣ Prepare the Peppercorn Sauce  Finely chop your onion, garlic and fresh rosemary. Make sure your black pepper is coarsely ground rather than finely powdered. We want that beautiful peppercorn flavour and texture, not a mouthful of pepper dust. 💀 Combine the cream, black pepper, onion, garlic, rosemary, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar and mustard. Give everything a good mix and set aside. 3️⃣ Prepare the Potato Wedges  Slice your potatoes into wedges, or whatever shape your heart desires. Add the paprika, onion powder, dried parsley, olive oil and salt. Mix everything thoroughly, making sure those potatoes are generously coated. Get them straight into a preheated oven or air fryer at 180°C until golden, crispy and cooked through, turning halfway. Don’t leave them sitting around after seasoning because the salt will start drawing moisture out of the potatoes. 🤓 4️⃣ Sear the Chicken  Heat a large pan over medium heat and place your marinated chicken thighs skin-side down. Let the skin slowly render its fat and develop a beautiful golden crust. Don’t rush this part! Good things take time, and crispy chicken skin is definitely one of them. Once nicely browned, flip the chicken and sear the other side for a few minutes. 5️⃣ Bring Everything Together  Pour approximately 1 cup of chicken stock or water into the pan. Now add your prepared creamy peppercorn mixture. Give everything a gentle stir, making sure all those browned bits from the bottom of the pan get incorporated into the sauce. Allow everything to simmer gently until the chicken is completely cooked through and the sauce has thickened beautifully. The chicken should reach an internal temperature of at least 75°C. Taste the sauce and adjust the seasoning if necessary. 6️⃣ Serve & Enjoy  Plate up your crispy potato wedges alongside those juicy chicken thighs. Now SMOTHER everything in that rich, creamy peppercorn sauce. Finish with a sprinkle of freshly chopped chives to make the whole thing healthy. 🙂 And there you have it. Chicken au poivre with a little extra personality. BON APPÉTIT, OR WHATEVER THE FRENCH SAY.

Marinate the chicken: Mix the chicken with paprika, black pepper, salt, garlic powder, onion powder and oil. Leave to marinate for 30 minutes. 2. Prepare the coating: Mix the flour with the same spices used for the marinade. Set up separate bowls of beaten eggs and panko breadcrumbs. 3. Coat and fry: Coat each chicken piece in flour, dip into the beaten eggs, then coat generously in panko breadcrumbs. Deep-fry on medium heat for 7–8 minutes, or until golden, crispy and fully cooked through. 4. Make the Caesar dressing: Mix mayonnaise, mustard, garlic, black pepper, garlic powder, salt, Parmesan and olive oil. Gradually add water until you reach your desired consistency. 5. Prepare the salad: Reserve some dressing for the burgers and serving. Toss the remaining dressing with the romaine lettuce. 6. Assemble: Spread Caesar dressing on the burger bun, add the crispy chicken, followed by the Caesar salad and freshly grated Parmesan. In a large bowl, combine the chicken thighs with olive oil, garlic, sofrito, Loisa Adobo, garlic powder, annatto powder, oregano, parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix well so every piece is evenly coated. Arrange chicken in a baking dish and cover tightly with foil. Bake for 1 hour. Carefully remove the foil and return to the oven for 5-10 minutes to develop a beautiful golden color and slightly crispy skin. Let rest for a few minutes before serving. Serve and enjoy!
